outcomes.text: identify God’s purpose for his or her life to live meaningfully
narrate the parable of the talents
apply lessons learnt from the parable in their day-to-day life
participate in different activities to nurture their talents, gifts and abilities. Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Suggested

skills.name: Know the parable of the talents (Matthew 25:14-30) and what it teaches
skills.mastery: Says that the master gave five, two and one talents, each according to ability; that the first two servants used theirs and gained more; that the third buried his; that the master praised the faithful servants; and that the lesson is to use what God has given. Does not read the talents as only money or say the master was unfair. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: recall a fact of the parable
say why the third servant was blamed

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Know what Jeremiah 29:11, James 1:17 and 1 Peter 4:10 say about God's purpose and gifts
skills.mastery: Says that God has plans for the child's welfare, future and hope (Jeremiah 29:11), that every good gift comes from God (James 1:17) and that each person should use the gift received to serve others (1 Peter 4:10). Does not say that gifts are for showing off or only for adults. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: match a verse to its message
choose the response that fits the verse

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the lesson is only about money.

example.question: What does the parable of the talents teach a Grade 5 learner?
example.wrong_answer: Keep your money safe and never spend it
example.correct_answer: Use the gifts and abilities God has given you

misconceptions.cause: A talent in the story was a large sum of money, so the child reads the story as advice about savings.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Keep your money safe and never spend it" beside "Use the gifts and abilities God has given you" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask what the servants did with what they were given. Then name other gifts: singing, kindness, farming, drawing, helping.
misconceptions.feedback: In the story a talent was a sum of money, but Jesus told it to teach us to use every gift and ability God gives us, not only money.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the master was unfair, or that the third servant was punished for having least.

example.question: Why was the third servant blamed?
example.wrong_answer: He was given less than the others
example.correct_answer: He buried his talent and did not use it

misconceptions.cause: The child notices the amounts (five, two, one) and thinks that having less is the fault.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "He was given less than the others" beside "He buried his talent and did not use it" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Reread Matthew 25:15, "each according to his ability", then the servant's own words about fear and the buried talent.
misconceptions.feedback: The master gave each servant a share to match his ability. The third servant was blamed because he buried his talent and did not use it, not because he was given less.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes up the numbers of talents given and gained.

example.question: How many talents did the first servant gain?
example.correct_answer: Five more

misconceptions.cause: The child remembers five, two and one but not which servant gained what.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Two more" beside "Five more" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Draw three columns: given, gained, total. Fill them from Matthew 25:16-18.
misconceptions.feedback: The servant who was given five talents gained five more, the one given two gained two more, and the one given one buried it and gained nothing.
misconceptions.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

misconceptions.error: Thinks gifts are given so that a person can be admired or win.

example.question: According to 1 Peter 4:10, what should each person do with the gift received?
example.wrong_answer: Show it off so others admire you
example.correct_answer: Use it to serve others

misconceptions.cause: Children see talent shows and prizes and link gifts to winning.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Show it off so others admire you" beside "Use it to serve others" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Peter 4:10 aloud and ask who benefits when a gift is used to serve.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 Peter 4:10 says each person should use the gift received to serve others, as a good steward of God's grace. A gift is for service, not for showing off.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks God has a purpose only for adults or only for people with big talents.

example.question: What does Jeremiah 29:11 say about God's plans?
example.wrong_answer: God has plans only for adults
example.correct_answer: God has plans for welfare, a future and hope

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks purpose belongs to jobs and grown-ups.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "God has plans only for adults" beside "God has plans for welfare, a future and hope" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Jeremiah 29:11 and ask who God is speaking about. Say that a Grade 5 child is included.
misconceptions.feedback: Jeremiah 29:11 says that God has plans for our welfare, to give us a future and a hope. A child is part of that, not only an adult.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a person's abilities come only from the person's own effort.

example.question: According to James 1:17, where does every good gift come from?
example.wrong_answer: From a person's own hard work alone
example.correct_answer: From God, the Father of lights

misconceptions.cause: Effort is praised at school, so the giver is forgotten.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "From a person's own hard work alone" beside "From God, the Father of lights" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read James 1:17. Say that work matters, but that the ability to work and learn is a gift too.
misconceptions.feedback: James 1:17 says that every good and perfect gift comes from above, from God. Hard work matters, but the abilities we work with are gifts too.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

Why is child labour an abuse of the rights of a child?

outcomes.text: identify three responsibilities given to human beings by God
demonstrate good stewardship by taking care of God’s creation
outline their roles at home, school and church
explain the causes of child labour today
explain the effects of child labour for protection of self and others
desire to engage in age-appropriate tasks/chores

skills.name: Know the work God gave human beings and the roles at home, school and church
skills.mastery: Names the responsibilities in Genesis 1:26 and 2:15 (rule over, look after, till and keep the garden) and tells caring for creation from using it up. Gives roles a child really has at home, at school and at church. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: a role at home, school or church

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Tell child labour from age-appropriate chores, with its causes, effects and where to report
skills.mastery: Separates child labour (work that is heavy, harmful, or keeps a child from school) from light chores that suit a child's age; gives causes (poverty, ignorance, greed of employers, loss of parents) and effects (missing school, harm to health, loss of play and safety); and names safe people to report to (a parent or guardian, a teacher, the chief, a children's officer or the Childline Kenya helpline 116). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Reads "rule over" in Genesis 1:26 as permission to use up or harm creation.

example.question: What does it mean to rule over the animals and plants in Genesis 1:26 and 2:15?
example.wrong_answer: Use them as we like, even if they are finished
example.correct_answer: Look after them as God's caretaker

misconceptions.cause: The word rule is heard as power, not as care.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Use them as we like, even if they are finished" beside "Look after them as God's caretaker" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 2:15 beside it: "to work it and take care of it".
misconceptions.feedback: Genesis 2:15 shows what ruling means: to work the garden and take care of it. Human beings are God's caretakers of creation, not owners who may use it up.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks work is only a punishment.

example.question: When did God first give human beings work in the Bible?
example.wrong_answer: After they did wrong, as a punishment
example.correct_answer: In the garden, before they did wrong

misconceptions.cause: Work is hard at times, so the child thinks it began as a punishment.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "After they did wrong, as a punishment" beside "In the garden, before they did wrong" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Compare Genesis 2:15 (work in the garden) with Genesis 3.
misconceptions.feedback: In Genesis 2:15 God put the man in the garden to work it and take care of it before anything went wrong. Work is a good gift and a responsibility.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a child has a role only at home.

example.question: Which one is a role a child can do at church?
example.correct_answer: Helping to keep the church compound clean

misconceptions.cause: The child lists chores for home and misses school and church roles.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Cleaning the compound at home" beside "Helping to keep the church compound clean" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Make three lists on the board: home, school and church.
misconceptions.feedback: A child has roles at home, school and church. At church a child can sing, help as an usher, sweep, and help keep the compound clean.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks every chore at home is child labour.

example.question: Which of these is child labour?
example.correct_answer: Carrying heavy loads for hours instead of going to school

misconceptions.cause: The child hears that work for children is wrong and applies it to every chore.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Sweeping the room after school" beside "Carrying heavy loads for hours instead of going to school" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Sort tasks by three questions: is it safe, does it suit my age, does it stop me from school or rest?
misconceptions.feedback: Light chores that suit your age, such as sweeping or washing dishes, are good training. Child labour is work that is harmful or takes a child away from school, rest and play.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks child labour is good because it teaches a child to work or earns money.

example.question: What is a common effect of child labour?
example.wrong_answer: The child learns more at school
example.correct_answer: The child misses school and can be hurt

misconceptions.cause: The child links any work with growing up well.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The child learns more at school" beside "The child misses school and can be hurt" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Name a child who herds all day and cannot read. Ask what the child lost.
misconceptions.feedback: Child labour takes children from school and can harm their health and safety. Learning to work happens through safe chores, not through harmful work.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a child forced to work should tell the employer or keep quiet.

example.question: Whom should a child tell if he is forced to work?
example.correct_answer: A trusted adult such as a teacher, the chief or a parent

misconceptions.cause: The child fears the person in charge.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The person who forces him" beside "A trusted adult such as a teacher, the chief or a parent" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Make a list of safe adults together, including the Childline Kenya line 116.
misconceptions.feedback: A child who is forced to work should tell a trusted adult such as a parent, a teacher or the chief, or call the Childline Kenya helpline on 116. Not the person who is forcing the work.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Blames the child or says children work only because they are lazy at school.

example.question: What is one cause of child labour in many places?
example.wrong_answer: Children who like to be lazy
example.correct_answer: Poverty in the family

misconceptions.cause: The child blames the child instead of the conditions.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Children who like to be lazy" beside "Poverty in the family" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask what a family with no food might feel it must do.
misconceptions.feedback: Child labour is often caused by poverty, the loss of parents, ignorance of children's rights and the greed of those who use cheap labour. It is not the fault of the child.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

outline five lessons learnt from the fall of man

skills.name: Know the story of the fall of man (Genesis 3:1-11) and its lessons
skills.mastery: Says that the serpent tempted the woman, that she and the man ate from the tree God had forbidden, that they hid when they heard God, and that God asked "Where are you?"; and states lessons: obey God, do not blame others, wrong choices have results. Does not say the Bible names the fruit. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: recall a fact of the story

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Says the fruit was an apple.

example.question: What does Genesis 3 say about the kind of fruit that was eaten?
example.correct_answer: The Bible does not name the fruit

misconceptions.cause: Pictures and stories name the fruit, and the child remembers the picture.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It was an apple" beside "The Bible does not name the fruit" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:6 and look for the name of the fruit together.
misconceptions.feedback: Genesis 3 says "the fruit of the tree" but does not name it. The apple comes from pictures and stories, not from the Bible.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks only one person ate or that the other was not involved.

example.question: Who ate the fruit God had forbidden?
example.correct_answer: The woman, who then gave some to her husband, and he ate

misconceptions.cause: The child remembers the woman and the serpent but not the man.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only the woman" beside "The woman, who then gave some to her husband, and he ate" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:6 and count who ate.
misconceptions.feedback: In Genesis 3:6 the woman ate the fruit and she also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate. Both disobeyed God.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the serpent told the truth or was a friend.

example.question: What did the serpent do?
example.wrong_answer: He told them the truth about God
example.correct_answer: He tempted them to doubt what God said

misconceptions.cause: The child follows the serpent's smooth words in the story.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "He told them the truth about God" beside "He tempted them to doubt what God said" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Compare what God said in Genesis 2:17 with what the serpent said in 3:4.
misconceptions.feedback: The serpent made the woman doubt what God had said. He tempted them, and what he said was not true.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks blaming someone else is an acceptable answer to wrong done.

example.question: After eating the fruit, the man blamed the woman. What should a person do when he does wrong?
example.correct_answer: Admit it honestly and say sorry

misconceptions.cause: The child sees blame as a way out, as the man did.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Blame someone else" beside "Admit it honestly and say sorry" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:12-13 and ask whether blaming helped.
misconceptions.feedback: Adam blamed Eve and Eve blamed the serpent. Blaming others does not remove our own wrong. A person should admit what he did and say sorry.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

explain the importance of family unity,

How can family unity be maintained?

outcomes.text: describe the importance of family unity
identify challenges faced by families today
outline ways he/she can contribute to a happy family
take part in doing simple chores at home

skills.name: Know why family unity matters, its challenges and how a child helps (Colossians 3:13-14)
skills.mastery: Gives reasons family unity matters (love, help, peace, safety), names challenges families face (quarrels, poverty, illness, long absence, unkind words), and gives ways a child helps (forgiving, doing chores, speaking kindly, obeying). Knows that Colossians 3:13-14 speaks of bearing with one another, forgiving and love. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a united family never disagrees.

example.question: What is family unity?
example.correct_answer: Living together in love, helping and forgiving one another

misconceptions.cause: The child sees unity as the absence of noise.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Never disagreeing about anything" beside "Living together in love, helping and forgiving one another" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Colossians 3:13-14: bear with each other and forgive. That assumes there are things to forgive.
misconceptions.feedback: A united family has disagreements too, but its members forgive each other and keep loving one another (Colossians 3:13-14).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks only parents are responsible for a happy family.

example.question: Who can help to make a family happy?
example.correct_answer: Every member of the family, including children

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks children only receive.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only the parents" beside "Every member of the family, including children" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List three things a child can do: chores, kind words, obedience.
misconceptions.feedback: Every member of the family, including children, can help to make a family happy by obeying, doing chores and speaking kindly.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks forgiving means pretending nothing happened or that wrong was right.

example.question: What does it mean to forgive a family member?
example.wrong_answer: To pretend nothing wrong was done
example.correct_answer: To let go of the anger and choose to love again

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes forgiving with ignoring.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "To pretend nothing wrong was done" beside "To let go of the anger and choose to love again" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say what Colossians 3:13 asks: forgive as the Lord forgave you.
misconceptions.feedback: To forgive is to let go of anger and choose to love again. It does not pretend that nothing was wrong.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

outcomes.text: outline different uses of the Bible in society today
identify the benefits of reading the Bible
read the Bible always to grow spiritually

skills.name: Know how the Bible guides and why Christians read it (Joshua 1:8, Psalm 1:1-3)
skills.mastery: Gives uses of the Bible in society (teaching right and wrong, comfort, guidance, worship, prayer, oaths on some occasions, moral teaching in schools) and benefits of reading it (growing in faith, wisdom, strength, direction). Knows that Joshua 1:8 and Psalm 1:1-3 speak of meditating on God's word and its blessing. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Bible is useful only inside church.

example.question: Where does the Bible guide a Christian?
example.correct_answer: At home, school, church and in the community every day

misconceptions.cause: The child meets the Bible mostly in church.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only at church on Sunday" beside "At home, school, church and in the community every day" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask for a verse that helps at home or at school.
misconceptions.feedback: The Bible guides a Christian in every place and every day: at home, at school, at church and in the community.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks reading the Bible once is enough.

example.question: What does Joshua 1:8 ask about God's word?
example.wrong_answer: Read it once and then keep it safe
example.correct_answer: Think about it day and night and do what it says

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks of reading as finishing a book.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Read it once and then keep it safe" beside "Think about it day and night and do what it says" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Joshua 1:8 and Psalm 1:2, "his delight is in the law of the Lord".
misconceptions.feedback: Joshua 1:8 asks us to think on God's word day and night and to do what it says. It is for daily use, not for reading once.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not know what Psalm 1:1-3 compares the person who loves God's word to.

example.question: In Psalm 1:3, the person who delights in God's word is like...
example.correct_answer: A tree planted by streams of water

misconceptions.cause: The child remembers an image from the Bible but not which.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "A strong wall" beside "A tree planted by streams of water" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Psalm 1:3 and draw the tree.
misconceptions.feedback: Psalm 1:3 says that the person who delights in the word of the Lord is like a tree planted by streams of water, which gives fruit in its season.
misconceptions.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

skills.name: Know the story of Peter and John before the rulers (Acts 4) and why Christians stand firm
skills.mastery: Says that Peter and John were arrested for teaching about Jesus, were questioned about the power by which a man had been healed, that Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, spoke boldly, that he said there is salvation in no other name than Jesus (Acts 4:12), and that the rulers saw their courage and knew they had been with Jesus. Gives a reason to stand firm. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: recall a fact of the story

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Mixes this story with Peter denying Jesus and thinks Peter was afraid to speak.

example.question: How did Peter speak to the rulers in Acts 4?
example.wrong_answer: He was afraid and said he did not know Jesus
example.correct_answer: He spoke boldly, filled with the Holy Spirit

misconceptions.cause: The child remembers Peter's denial in the courtyard.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "He was afraid and said he did not know Jesus" beside "He spoke boldly, filled with the Holy Spirit" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Acts 4:8 and 4:13: "filled with the Holy Spirit", "the courage of Peter and John".
misconceptions.feedback: In Acts 4 Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke boldly. That is different from the night when he denied Jesus.
misconceptions.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

misconceptions.error: Thinks Peter and John promised to stop speaking about Jesus.

example.question: What did Peter say about salvation in Acts 4:12?
example.wrong_answer: That there are many ways and names
example.correct_answer: That there is no salvation in any other name than Jesus

misconceptions.cause: The child expects the story to end with the apostles giving in.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "That there are many ways and names" beside "That there is no salvation in any other name than Jesus" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Acts 4:12 aloud, then verse 13.
misconceptions.feedback: Acts 4:12 says that there is salvation in no one else, and no other name under heaven by which we must be saved. Peter did not give in.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks that Peter and John did the healing by their own power.

example.question: By whose power did Peter say the man had been healed?
example.wrong_answer: By the power of Peter and John
example.correct_answer: By the name of Jesus Christ

misconceptions.cause: The child sees the apostles as the actors and forgets the power given.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "By the power of Peter and John" beside "By the name of Jesus Christ" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Acts 4:10.
misconceptions.feedback: Peter told the rulers that the man was healed by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. The apostles gave the glory to Jesus.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

skills.name: Know the story of Solomon and the two women (1 Kings 3:16-28) and what it teaches
skills.mastery: Says that two women claimed one living baby, that Solomon called for a sword to divide the child, that the real mother gave up her claim to save the child, and that Solomon gave the baby to her. Gives lessons (wisdom, listening to both sides, love shows in giving) and what Proverbs 9:10 says. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: recall a fact of the story
a lesson or a wise choice

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the woman who agreed to divide the child was the real mother.

example.question: Which woman did Solomon decide was the real mother?
example.correct_answer: The woman who said, "Give her the living child"

misconceptions.cause: The child follows the first voice and misses the love in giving up.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The woman who said, "Divide him"" beside "The woman who said, "Give her the living child"" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Reread 1 Kings 3:26-27 and ask who loved the child.
misconceptions.feedback: The real mother loved her son so much that she begged the king to give him to the other woman rather than see him killed. So Solomon gave the baby to her.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks Solomon really had the baby cut in two.

example.question: What happened to the baby?
example.wrong_answer: Solomon had him cut in two
example.correct_answer: He was given to his real mother alive

misconceptions.cause: The child misses that the order was a test.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Solomon had him cut in two" beside "He was given to his real mother alive" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read verse 27: "Give her the living child".
misconceptions.feedback: The sword was never used. Solomon's order was a test to find out who the real mother was, and the baby was given to her alive.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks Solomon's wisdom meant strength, riches or force.

example.question: What does Proverbs 9:10 say is the beginning of wisdom?
example.correct_answer: Respect and reverence for the Lord

misconceptions.cause: The child sees a king and pictures power.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Having riches and power" beside "Respect and reverence for the Lord" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Proverbs 9:10 and ask what Solomon asked from God in 1 Kings 3:9.
misconceptions.feedback: Proverbs 9:10 says that the fear of the Lord, that is, deep respect for God, is the beginning of wisdom. It is not riches or power.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

skills.name: Know the story of Noah and his sons (Genesis 9:18-23)
skills.mastery: Names Shem, Ham and Japheth as the sons of Noah who came out of the ark; says that Noah planted a vineyard, drank wine and lay uncovered in his tent; that Ham told his brothers; and that Shem and Japheth covered their father without looking. Does not mix up the sons with other Bible brothers. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Know ways of showing respect to the elderly
skills.mastery: Gives ways of showing respect to older people (greeting politely, listening, helping with loads and chores, giving a seat, speaking kindly, visiting) and does not think respect means agreeing with everything or only applies to relatives. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: what to do in a situation

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Gives wrong names for Noah's sons.

example.question: Which are the names of Noah's three sons?
example.correct_answer: Shem, Ham and Japheth

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes the first sons in Genesis with those after the flood.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Cain, Abel and Seth" beside "Shem, Ham and Japheth" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 9:18 and write the three names on a card.
misconceptions.feedback: Genesis 9:18 names Noah's sons who came out of the ark as Shem, Ham and Japheth.
misconceptions.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

misconceptions.error: Thinks Ham covered his father.

example.question: Which sons covered their father with a garment?
example.correct_answer: Shem and Japheth

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes who saw with who covered.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Ham" beside "Shem and Japheth" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 9:22-23 slowly, naming each son.
misconceptions.feedback: Ham saw his father and told his brothers outside. Shem and Japheth took a garment and covered their father, walking backwards so that they did not see him.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the story is about the flood itself.

example.question: What is the story in Genesis 9:18-23 mostly about?
example.correct_answer: How Noah's sons treated their father

misconceptions.cause: The child knows Noah from the ark and the flood.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "How Noah built the ark" beside "How Noah's sons treated their father" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say that the flood is over in this reading.
misconceptions.feedback: In Genesis 9:18-23 the flood is already over. The story is about how Noah's sons treated their father after he lay uncovered in his tent.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks respect means agreeing with everything an older person says.

example.question: Which shows respect to an older person?
example.wrong_answer: Agreeing with everything and never asking a question
example.correct_answer: Greeting politely and listening carefully

misconceptions.cause: The child confuses respect with silence.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Agreeing with everything and never asking a question" beside "Greeting politely and listening carefully" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask whether a polite question is respectful.
misconceptions.feedback: Respect is shown by polite words and actions: greeting, listening, helping. It does not mean never speaking.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks respect is only for relatives.

example.question: To whom should a child show respect?
example.correct_answer: Every older person, including neighbours and strangers

misconceptions.cause: The child ties respect to the family.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only grandparents and relatives" beside "Every older person, including neighbours and strangers" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Give a story of an older neighbour carrying water.
misconceptions.feedback: A child shows respect to every older person: grandparents, neighbours, teachers and elders in the community.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks you help an older person only if you are paid or thanked.

example.question: Why do Christians respect and help the elderly?
example.wrong_answer: So that they pay or reward us
example.correct_answer: Because it pleases God and is the right thing to do

misconceptions.cause: The child does tasks for rewards.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "So that they pay or reward us" beside "Because it pleases God and is the right thing to do" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask what Shem and Japheth gained.
misconceptions.feedback: Christians respect and help the elderly because it is right and pleases God, not to gain a reward.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

skills.name: Know the story of the hand that wrote on the wall (Daniel 5)
skills.mastery: Says that King Belshazzar held a feast and used the gold and silver vessels from the temple in Jerusalem, that a human hand wrote on the wall, that no wise man could read it, that Daniel was called and read it, and that the writing said the kingdom had been counted, weighed and divided. Gives lessons (do not misuse holy things, pride has a price, God is above kings). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: recall a fact of the story

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Know what humility is and how Daniel showed it
skills.mastery: Describes humility as thinking rightly of yourself and others, without boasting; gives benefits (peace, learning, friends, honour from God and people) and tells Daniel's quiet, faithful service from the proud king's behaviour. Does not say that humility means being weak or having no opinion. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Names the wrong king.

example.question: Which king held the feast in Daniel 5?
example.correct_answer: Belshazzar

misconceptions.cause: Nebuchadnezzar is better known.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Nebuchadnezzar" beside "Belshazzar" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Daniel 5:1 and write the name.
misconceptions.feedback: The king who held the feast in Daniel 5 was Belshazzar. Nebuchadnezzar had taken the vessels from the temple earlier.
misconceptions.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

misconceptions.error: Thinks Daniel wrote the words or that a person wrote them.

example.question: Whose hand wrote on the wall?
example.correct_answer: A human hand that appeared, with no body

misconceptions.cause: The child skips the first lines of the passage.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Daniel's hand" beside "A human hand that appeared, with no body" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Daniel 5:5.
misconceptions.feedback: In Daniel 5:5 the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the wall. Daniel did not write them. He was called to read and explain them.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the holy vessels were used well at the feast.

example.question: Why was it wrong to use the gold and silver vessels at the feast?
example.wrong_answer: They were too heavy to carry
example.correct_answer: They were holy vessels from God's temple and were used to drink wine and praise idols

misconceptions.cause: The child sees a feast but not the insult to God.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "They were too heavy to carry" beside "They were holy vessels from God's temple and were used to drink wine and praise idols" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Daniel 5:2-4.
misconceptions.feedback: The vessels belonged to the temple in Jerusalem and were holy to God. Belshazzar used them at his feast while praising idols of gold and silver.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not know what the writing said.

example.question: What did the writing say about the king's kingdom?
example.correct_answer: It was numbered, weighed and divided

misconceptions.cause: The child does not follow the three words.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It would grow bigger" beside "It was numbered, weighed and divided" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Daniel 5:25-28 and match mene, tekel and peres.
misconceptions.feedback: Daniel said that God had numbered the kingdom and ended it, that the king had been weighed and found too light, and that the kingdom would be divided.
misconceptions.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

misconceptions.error: Thinks humility means being weak or thinking nothing of yourself.

example.question: What is humility?
example.wrong_answer: Being weak and having no opinions
example.correct_answer: Not boasting, and treating others with respect

misconceptions.cause: The child hears humble and thinks of poor or small.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Being weak and having no opinions" beside "Not boasting, and treating others with respect" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask whether Daniel was weak when he spoke to the king.
misconceptions.feedback: Humility is not weakness. A humble person does not boast, listens, and treats others with respect. Daniel spoke truthfully to a king.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the king was humble.

example.question: Who showed pride in the story?
example.correct_answer: King Belshazzar

misconceptions.cause: The child misreads who did what.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Daniel" beside "King Belshazzar" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Daniel 5:22-23, where Daniel says Belshazzar did not humble himself.
misconceptions.feedback: Daniel told the king that he had not humbled himself but had lifted himself up against God. King Belshazzar showed pride, not Daniel.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks Daniel served the king for a reward.

example.question: What did Daniel say to the king's gifts and rewards?
example.correct_answer: He said the king could keep the gifts, and he read the writing anyway

misconceptions.cause: The child expects the hero to get paid.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "He asked for more rewards" beside "He said the king could keep the gifts, and he read the writing anyway" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Daniel 5:17.
misconceptions.feedback: In Daniel 5:17 Daniel said the king could keep his gifts and give his rewards to someone else, yet he would still read the writing. He served God faithfully, not for pay.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

skills.name: Know the contest on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:22-39) and what it teaches
skills.mastery: Says that Elijah stood alone against 450 prophets of Baal, that each side prepared a bull and no one lit the fire, that Baal did not answer, that Elijah prayed and the fire of the Lord fell, and that the people said the Lord is God. Gives lessons (worship God alone, trust in prayer, courage to stand alone). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: recall a fact of the contest

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Tell the true God from false gods and know why worship belongs to God alone
skills.mastery: Tells the Lord who answered by fire from idols that cannot hear, see or speak; knows that the Ten Commandments forbid worshipping other gods and making idols to bow down to; and chooses a safe response when a group or friend invites a child to worship or follow something against these teachings. Never judges other people by name. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: what to do when invited to a harmful group

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Baal answered first.

example.question: What happened when the prophets of Baal called on Baal?
example.correct_answer: There was no answer

misconceptions.cause: The child expects both sides to be equal.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Baal sent fire" beside "There was no answer" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Kings 18:26, "there was no voice".
misconceptions.feedback: The prophets of Baal called from morning till noon and there was no voice and no answer. Only the Lord answered by fire.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks Elijah lit the fire.

example.question: Who sent the fire onto Elijah's altar?
example.correct_answer: The Lord sent it from heaven

misconceptions.cause: The child pictures a prophet and not the Lord acting.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Elijah lit it himself" beside "The Lord sent it from heaven" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read verse 38: "the fire of the Lord fell".
misconceptions.feedback: The fire of the Lord fell and burned up the offering, the wood, the stones and the dust, and even the water in the trench. Elijah did not light it.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes up the numbers.

example.question: How many prophets of Baal were there on Mount Carmel?
example.correct_answer: Twelve

misconceptions.cause: Numbers in the story: 450 prophets, twelve stones, four jars of water.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Four hundred and fifty" beside "Twelve" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Make a card for each number and what it counted.
misconceptions.feedback: There were 450 prophets of Baal against Elijah alone. The twelve stones stood for the twelve tribes, and Elijah had jars of water poured on the altar.
misconceptions.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

misconceptions.error: Thinks an idol can hear and help.

example.question: What can an idol made of wood or stone do?
example.correct_answer: Nothing, because it cannot hear, see or speak

misconceptions.cause: The child hears about gods in some stories as strong.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Hear prayers and answer them" beside "Nothing, because it cannot hear, see or speak" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Compare Carmel: the idol did not answer, the Lord did.
misconceptions.feedback: An idol cannot hear, see, speak or answer. At Carmel the Lord answered and Baal did not. God alone is worthy of worship.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a group that asks for secrecy and harmful acts is safe to join.

example.question: A group tells Mwende to join secret meetings and not to tell her parents. What should she do?
example.correct_answer: Tell her parents or a trusted adult and not join

misconceptions.cause: The child values belonging and trusts a friendly invitation.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Join, because they are friendly" beside "Tell her parents or a trusted adult and not join" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say that secrets from parents are a warning sign.
misconceptions.feedback: A group that asks a child to hide things from her parents, or to do something against God's teaching, is unsafe. Mwende should refuse and tell her parents or a trusted adult.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks a Christian can worship the Lord and other gods together.

example.question: What do the Ten Commandments say about other gods?
example.wrong_answer: Worship the Lord and also other gods
example.correct_answer: Do not have other gods before the Lord, and do not make idols to bow down to

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks worship can be shared.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Worship the Lord and also other gods" beside "Do not have other gods before the Lord, and do not make idols to bow down to" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Exodus 20:3-5 and ask what Elijah said to the people in 1 Kings 18:21.

skills.mastery: Names substances young people misuse (alcohol, bhang, miraa, cigarettes, glue and petrol sniffing), tells misuse from medicine taken as a health worker directs, gives reasons young people start (peer pressure, stress, curiosity, copying adults), effects (poor health, failing school, quarrels, crime, addiction) and values that help (self-control, courage, honesty, wisdom). example.wrong_answer: Taking medicine as the doctor says
example.correct_answer: Sniffing glue to feel different

misconceptions.cause: The child hears drug and thinks of anything swallowed.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Taking medicine as the doctor says" beside "Sniffing glue to feel different" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask the difference between medicine given by a nurse and a pill taken for fun.
misconceptions.feedback: Medicine taken as a health worker directs is not drug abuse. Drug abuse is using a substance such as alcohol, bhang or glue in a way that harms the body and mind.

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only adults" beside "Both adults and children, especially when friends pressure them" and ask the child to choose.

misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks trying a drug once will do no harm.

misconceptions.help: Say that many people started with one try.
misconceptions.feedback: Even one try can start a habit that is hard to stop. Proverbs 20:1 warns that strong drink leads people astray.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks drugs make a person stronger or better at school.

indicators.indicator: Ability to list social media sites COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING AT UPPER PRIMARY (GRADE 4-6) At this level, the goal of the CSL activity is to provide linkages between concepts learnt in the various learning activities and the real-life experiences. Learners begin to make connections between what they learn and the relevance to their daily life. CSL is hosted in the Social Studies learning area. The implementation is a collaborative effort where the class teacher coordinates and works with other subject teachers to design and implement the integrated CSL activity. Though they are teacher-guided, the learners should progressively be given more autonomy to identify problems and come up with solutions. The safety of the learners should also be taken into account when selecting the CSL activity. The following steps for the integrated CSL activity should be staggered across the school terms: Steps in carrying out the integrated CSL activity 1. Preparation ● Map out the targeted core competencies, values and specific learning area skills for the CSL activity ● Identify resources required for the activity (locally available materials) ● Stagger the activities across the term (set dates and time for the activities) ● Communicate to learners, parents/caregivers/guardians, school administration, teachers and other relevant stakeholders in the school community ● Identify and develop assessment tools 2. Implementation of the CSL Activity ● Assign roles to learners. ● Ensure every learner actively participates in the activity ● Observe learners as they carry out the CSL activity and record feedback ● Use an appropriate assessment tool to assess both the process and the product (assess learner’s work from the beginning to the end product) ● Assess the targeted core competencies, values and subject skills. 3. Reflection on the CSL Activity Conduct a self-evaluation session with learners on the integrated CSL activity undertaken by discussing the following: ● what went well and why ● what did not go well and why ● what can be done differently next time ● what they have learnt. There will be one integrated CSL activity that will be conducted annually. The thematic areas for the integrated CSL activity will be derived from the broader categories of the PCIs and concepts from the various learning areas. Teachers are expected to vary the themes yearly to allow learners to address different PCIs within their contexts. There should be a linkage between the skills from the learning areas and the themes. The integrated CSL activity will take a Whole School Approach (WSA) where the entire school community is involved (learners, parents/caregivers/guardians, school administration, teachers). Parents/caregivers/guardians are key stakeholders in the planning and execution of the CSL activity. Although the teacher takes the lead role in the planning and integration of the CSL activity, learners will be expected to participate actively in the whole process. The CSL activity provides an opportunity for the development of core competencies and the nurturing of various values. The teacher is expected to vary the core competencies and values emphasised in the activity yearly. Assessment of the CSL Activity Assessment of the integrated CSL activity will focus on 3 components namely: skills from various learning areas applied in carrying out the activity, and core competencies and values demonstrated. Assessment should focus on both the process and end product of the CSL activity. The teacher will assess learners in groups using various tools such as an observation schedule, checklist or rating scale or any other appropriate tool.
